assumptions.choice: Core position = entire available cash divided by close price, floored to the nearest 100 shares; the same formula is reused when re-entering the core long after forced assignment.
assumptions.reason: Spec offers 'entire capital or a fixed quantity, a multiple of 100' as an example; entire-capital sizing rounded to round lots is the most literal single choice covering both clauses.

assumptions.choice: Core position is bought on the first bar next() executes (after backtrader's automatic indicator warm-up), not at bar 1.
assumptions.reason: Canonical default #6 relies on automatic minperiod; price/indicator data is not reliably available inside __init__.

assumptions.choice: '20% of the current position' is computed off the live self.position.size at signal time, with a floor of 100 shares if position.size >= 100 else all available.
assumptions.reason: Literal reading of 'current position' plus the 'min 100 if available' qualifier.

assumptions.choice: Tracked as sum of currently active (not yet bought back) tranche quantities versus core_qty recorded at the most recent core entry; buybacks free up room.
assumptions.reason: Spec ties the cap to cumulative sold amount but also says buybacks 'restore the core position', implying capacity is regained.

assumptions.choice: Applied globally to any tranche-selling action (initial call-sale trigger and rolling add-on), not just the rolling clause.
assumptions.reason: Data is daily bars, so 'per day' naturally bounds all sell actions to avoid two conflicting sells on one bar; spec states it only under Rolling but the intent (rate-limiting sales) is general.

assumptions.choice: The mid-band/RSI<45 buyback trigger closes ALL currently active tranches at once, fully restoring the core position.
assumptions.reason: Spec explicitly says this action results in 'restoring the core position' (singular full outcome), not a partial buyback of one tranche.

assumptions.choice: If a tranche reaches its own 7-bar expiry and price is not above the upper band (roll condition fails), only that individual tranche is bought back, distinct from the broader mid-band/RSI<45 buyback-all trigger.
assumptions.reason: Spec only defines the roll branch explicitly for 'still above'; the implicit else (term ends, not ITM) most naturally closes just that expiring tranche.

assumptions.choice: 'After the sale' is read as: at least one tranche currently active/outstanding (self.tranches non-empty).
assumptions.reason: The clause only makes sense relative to a 'remaining position' that exists because shares were sold via a tranche.

assumptions.choice: At most one order-generating branch executes per bar (guarded by early returns and the pending-order tracker), even though multiple rule branches are evaluated in priority order each bar.
assumptions.reason: Prevents conflicting simultaneous buy/sell orders on the same bar given the spec describes several independent triggers with no defined precedence for simultaneous firing.

assumptions.choice: 'Close crosses above the upper band' implemented via CrossOver(close, bb.top), requiring the prior bar to be at/below the band.
assumptions.reason: Literal reading of 'crosses' as a transition event rather than a static 'is above' condition.
